newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cheered by rise in manufactured exports.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cheered by rise in manufactured exports.

text.p: A sharp year-on-year rise in exports of manufactured goods in June shows Brazil might not have to depend just on primary goods and world commodities prices to plug its burgeoning trade gap, officials said.

Mauricio Cortes, secretary of foreign trade in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce, said June's exports of $4.843 billion were "highly positive" and a rise in manufactured exports of 22.48 percent over June 1996 contributed significantly.
Brazil posted a $466 million trade deficit last month, bringing the first half trade gap to $4.71 billion compared with a $5.54 billion deficit for the whole of 1996.
Manufactured exports totaled $2.43 billion in June. Exports of primary goods were $1.638 billion, 44.19 percent higher than in June the year before.
"June has shown, perhaps for the first time, a significant expansion in manufactured exports," said Jose Roberto Mendonca de Barros, economic planning secretary at the Finance Ministry.

Mendonca de Barros said he did not know if that expansion would continue, but it showed Brazil might not have to depend just on higher commodities exports to improve its trade performance, "as some analysts have been suggesting".
The Finance Ministry official noted the mood on Brazil's external accounts had changed for the better and that there appeared to be an easing of pressures on the external accounts.

He said a group of eight independent consultants he met with on May 2 had predicted an average trade deficit for 1997 of $11.4 billion. At a subsequent meeting July 8, their average trade gap prediction had eased to $11.0 billion, he said.
Cortes said that exports in the third quarter of the year could be expected to remain relatively strong as the harvest would continue.
In the fourth quarter, the trade deficit could be expected to grow again, he said.
